sections.title: What your cleaning service invoice must show
sections.body: A generic bill causes confusion. Your invoice must clearly state the service location, especially if the billing address is different. You need distinct line items for labour, equipment fees, and consumables like bin liners or specialised floor treatments. If you provide staff cover for a commercial client, list the specific dates and hours worked. Always include your payment terms, bank details, and a clear due date. You can build a compliant document instantly using our free invoice generator at /tools/free-invoice-generator.

sections.title: How cleaning service work is priced and billed
sections.body: Cleaning businesses use several pricing models depending on the client. Commercial contracts are often priced per square metre and billed monthly in advance as a fixed retainer. Residential work is usually billed per visit or at an hourly rate. One-off jobs, like end-of-tenancy deep cleans or post-construction clearing, are typically billed on completion. Your invoice needs to reflect the exact pricing model you agreed upon. If you charge a flat rate but add extra fees for heavy soilage or oven cleaning, list these as separate line items so the client understands the total.
items: Per square metre for commercial spaces

sections.title: Getting paid: terms, deposits and chasing
sections.body: Cash flow is critical when you have staff to pay and supplies to buy. For large one-off jobs, always request a deposit before you schedule the work. State clearly on your invoice that the balance is due on completion. For recurring commercial contracts, standard terms are usually seven to fourteen days. Late payments happen, so you need a system to chase them. Send polite reminders a day after the due date. Clear payment instructions and a professional layout reduce delays and help you collect your money faster.

faqs.q: Should I charge for cleaning supplies separately?
faqs.a: It depends on your contract. Many residential cleaners include basic supplies in their hourly rate. However, for commercial contracts or specialised jobs, it is common to list consumables like paper towels, soap, and specific floor treatments as separate line items. This protects your profit margin if supply costs increase over time.

faqs.q: How do I bill for recurring monthly cleaning?
faqs.a: Set up a recurring invoice that goes out on the same day each month. Most commercial cleaning businesses bill monthly in advance for regular contracts. This ensures you have the funds to pay your staff and buy supplies for that month without waiting for clients to settle their accounts in arrears.

faqs.q: What is a staff cover charge?
faqs.a: A staff cover charge applies when you provide emergency personnel or extra cleaners outside the normal contract scope. You should list this clearly on the invoice, detailing the date, the number of staff provided, and the specific hours worked. This transparency prevents disputes when the client reviews their monthly bill.

faqs.q: Can I use this template for end-of-tenancy cleans?
faqs.a: Yes. End-of-tenancy cleans are usually one-off jobs billed on completion. You can use the template to list your flat rate for the core service, then add separate lines for extras like carpet shampooing, oven cleaning, or rubbish removal. Requesting a deposit before starting these heavy jobs is always a smart practice.
